Subject: Inference economics signal-check: hyperscaler cost probe & sample workload

Alex — thanks for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed probes so we can quantify the delta versus your hyperscaler baseline:

- Goal: establish per-1M token unit economics across three workload profiles (chat short, multi-turn assistant, long-context summarization) and measure latency percentile tradeoffs.
- Initial hypotheses from the call: Redwood can match latency at ~2–3x lower per-token cost with aggressive batching + KV-prefetching on your medium-length assistant workload; hyperscaler rates look competitive for short single-turn queries.

Next steps I propose (please confirm):
1) You share a sanitized sample_workload (JSON) and an expected QPS envelope for a 2-hour run.
2) Redwood runs a reproducible benchmark across the three profiles with cache-hit scenarios (cold, 30%, 70%) and returns per-1M token cost, p50/p95 latency, and CPU/GPU utilization.
3) We produce a short one-page executive delta (redwood vs hyperscaler) with assumptions and sensitivity to batching and cache hit.

Grace will be on the run and Marissa will own the measurement artifacts. Our attachments include a short benchmark guide (attached) — if you can drop the sample workload and procurement contact we’ll schedule the run.

Thanks,

Thanks — drafted the runbook and assumptions. Summary of the testing plan and quick guidance on what we'll report:

Planned test matrix (Jul 21 run):
- Profiles: chat-short, assistant-multi (6 turns), long-summary (2k tokens)
- Cache states: cold / 30% / 70%
- Load pattern: steady 50 qps + 2x 10-min spikes to 200 qps (as provided)
- Measurement windows: 30-minute steady-state samples per profile per cache state

What we'll report (per profile/cache):
- Raw tokens generated and consumed
- Total cost (compute + infra) and normalized per-1M tokens
- Latency p50/p95 and effective batching distribution
- Estimated hyperscaler unit cost (using public price + 20% discount) and percentage delta

Preliminary sensitivity (based on internal sims of similar workloads):
- Expected Redwood per-1M token: $9 — $34 (best case with 70% cache + large batching; worst case cold long-summary)
- Expected hyperscaler per-1M token: $28 — $120 (short queries skew low but long-context costs rise significantly)
- Key lever: cache hit rate and max-batch window — moving from 0% -> 70% hit reduces per-1M cost by ~55–65% on our stack for multi-turn workloads.

Deliverables after run:
- CSV: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_delta.csv (per-profile rows, costs, latency, utilization)
- One-page executive delta and runbook
- Raw logs and a reproducible script (Drive link) for Nimbus to rerun if desired

Questions/asks from us before run:
1) Confirm SSO/credentials to post results to your Drive folder (link in my outbound) or we can share a read-only link.
2) Let procurement know the test is non-billable research; if they require a DPA amendment or NDA note that to me.

Marissa will run the benchmark and Grace will track telemetry. If Jul 21 works we’ll start at 09:00 PST and post interim results by noon.

cheers,
Marissa Cole
